supported_claims: CausalDS provides narrated synthetic SCM scenes, data files, a separate observation model and private scoring artifacts.
Interventional and counterfactual targets have separate identification decisions, with abstention on nonidentifiable tasks.
The paper reports a 100-scene exam sampled from 953 scenes and finds that symbolic success, interval quality, abstention and cost can diverge.

inspected_anchors: PDF pp. 2, 4, 9: causal roadmap, eligibility and limitations
supported_claims: The proposed co-pilot follows a causal roadmap from the scientific question to assumptions, statistical estimands and interpretation.
Examples distinguish prevalent from incident users and specify eligibility, follow-up, baseline time, treatment and outcome; the paper discusses potentially time-varying exposure.
The authors find that careful cues help illustrative answers while off-the-shelf zero-shot responses may remain generic and miss relevant biases.

supported_claims: ARGUS audits reported evidence for DiD identifying assumptions and explicitly does not adjudicate causal truth.
The synthetic flaw study shows a retrieval/abstention trade-off: its gated pipeline misses some omissions that ungated ablations flag.
In the small five-paper human-label pilot, weak retrieval produces excessive severity; the reported calibration adjustment is in-sample and untested on unseen papers.

supported_claims: The population identification helper distinguishes identifiable true/false from unknown backend/error states.
It filters an IV estimand out of nonparametric population-ATE identification and can project explicit latent DAGs to y0 mixed graphs.
The README describes network-disabled task containers and separately network/model-enabled scene generation.
The grader gives abstention credit only for an explicitly abstainable task and an intentional null-equivalent response; malformed answers do not earn abstention credit.
The interval grader records width and coverage as well as an interval score; summary normalized interval scores are capped at 10.
The inspected helpers default missing identification metadata toward identifiable/not-nonidentifiable. The ATE interval branch checks ordering but does not explicitly reject every nonfinite endpoint.
limitations: High-priority benchmark candidate after auditing scorer, observation-model semantics and original data/assumption identities.
Do not turn missing-backend unknown into nonidentification; preserve conceptual versus proxy variables.
No local reproduction or container-conformance claim yet.
